subject.title: [Bug] Dreaming narrative: hardcoded 60s timeout includes lane-queue wait; timeout disposal aborts the primary call then discards the successful fallback-model output

question: What permanent Dream Diary timeout and cleanup contract should memory-core expose for queued narrative runs and late successful model output?
rationale: The source confirms a real bug shape, but the repair changes public plugin config/defaults and the semantics of cancelling or accepting in-flight narrative work after timeout.

options.title: Adopt a broader narrative lifecycle contract
options.body: Wire supported timeout config, make queue/execution timing explicit, and decide how late successful output is written or intentionally discarded with matching tests and docs.

options.title: Land timeout config only
options.body: Expose and wire timeoutMs first while leaving queue-time and late-output cleanup for a linked follow-up, accepting that this issue remains only partially solved.

options.title: Keep fixed fallback semantics
options.body: Decline configurable timeout and late-output preservation, document the fixed fallback behavior, and close this as intended behavior despite the reported operator impact.

recommendation.title: Adopt a broader narrative lifecycle contract
recommendation.body: Wire supported timeout config, make queue/execution timing explicit, and decide how late successful output is written or intentionally discarded with matching tests and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: The current timeout constant most directly traces to RayWoo's timeout behavior change, making them a good routing owner for the maintainer decision even though fallback/readback history is shared.
